newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parliament passes privatisation bill.
newsitem.headline: Polish parliament passes privatisation bill.

text.p: Poland's Parliament on Friday passed a bill allowing the government to quickly transform thousands of state firms into treasury-owned joint-stock companies and subject them to the commercial code.

The lower house rejected a Senate amendment to the measure, initially passed in June, under which privatisation of strategic sectors of the economy would be allowed only on the basis of separate parliamentary bills.
The law gives employees of privatised firms a right to get up to 15 percent of shares for free, rather than 20 percent at half-price as is now the case.
But the bill, despite pressure from some lobby groups, retains a limit on the value of shares that each worker can get, capping it at 18 average monthly wages in the enterprise sector.
The law will facilitate allocation of shares in companies to funds to be created under various government schemes.

The bill's critics say it will slow down privatisation because it would introduce more political patronage into the economy by allowing the ruling coalition to put its people on boards of firms being turned into joint-stock companies.
The bill has yet to be signed by President Aleksander Kwasniewski to become law.
